name: Breaking down complex goals into simpler steps
gist: Teaching agents to break large tasks into smaller subgoals or skills, and learning when and how to use each skill, so they can handle long-term, multi-step problems.
explain: Learning to do a simple task in one step is much easier than learning a ten-step task. If you ask a robot to assemble a toy, it's not learned anything useful if it only gets rewarded at the end — it has to connect actions ten steps ago to the final success. Hierarchical reinforcement learning breaks the problem into layers. The high-level layer learns the sequence of subgoals: pick up the part, position it, insert it, tighten it. The low-level layer learns how to execute each subgoal. The benefit: the high-level layer works with a simpler timeline (fewer decisions to connect), and the low-level layer can reuse skills across many high-level tasks.

The challenge is learning the right subgoals. If you ask the robot to learn 'position the part,' the robot has to figure out what 'positioned' means from experience. Papers here use techniques like skill discovery, where the system automatically identifies useful subgoals from trial data, or learning from demonstrations, where a human shows a few sequences and the system infers the subgoal structure. Some work on option frameworks — a reusable 'option' is a skill with a starting condition and an ending condition, and the agent learns which options to chain together.

Hierarchical learning matters for long-horizon tasks that humans solve naturally by chunking: cooking (gather ingredients, prep, cook, plate), building (design, source materials, assemble, test), or any multi-step process. Breaking it into layers lets agents learn much harder tasks.

papers.title: Action-Sufficient Goal Representations
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that action-sufficient representations consistently outperform value-derived representations, with up to 5.42 percentage-point gain on math tasks with 64 demonstrations.

papers.title: Bottleneck-Guided Spectral Subgoals For Offline Goal-Conditioned RL
papers.contribution: Proves routing through spectral bottlenecks yields approximately optimal one-step subgoals in terms of hitting-time under metastable decomposition.

papers.title: Goal Reaching with Eikonal-Constrained Hierarchical Quasimetric Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on offline goal-conditioned navigation and consistent gains over QRL in manipulation, matching temporal-difference methods.

papers.title: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Sparse-Reward Search in Commutative Algebra
papers.contribution: First application of hierarchical RL to commutative algebra, consistently outperforming classical RL and greedy search on Kalai's algebraic Hirsch conjecture.

papers.title: Leveraging Explanation to Improve Generalization of Meta Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Theoretically guarantees O(1/sqrt(K)) convergence and proves generalization improvement after task augmentation across MuJoCo and Meta-World experiments.

papers.title: RD-HRL: Generating Reliable Sub-Goals for Long-Horizon Sparse-Reward Tasks
papers.contribution: Outperforms baseline methods across multiple benchmarks for long-horizon sparse-reward tasks.

papers.title: SUSD: Structured Unsupervised Skill Discovery through State Factorization
papers.contribution: SUSD discovers richer, more complex and diverse skills across three environments with 1-10 factors, yielding factorized skill representations that enable efficient training of compositional downstream tasks via hierarchical RL.

papers.title: The State of Reinforcement Finetuning for Transformer-based Generative Agents
papers.contribution: Their empirical findings provide insights for advancing RFT effectiveness in meta-RL tasks, showing their lightweight enhancement consistently improves outcomes over standard approaches.

papers.title: APC-RL: Exceeding data-driven behavior priors with adaptive policy composition
papers.contribution: APC accelerates learning with aligned demonstrations, remains robust under severe misalignment, and leverages suboptimal demonstrations for exploration without performance degradation.

papers.title: Active Curriculum Refinement for Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Demonstrates strong robustness and generalization across diverse environments by leveraging the curriculum graph structure.

papers.title: Adaptive Policy Backbone via Shared Network
papers.contribution: Achieves comparable performance to standard RL while improving generalization to out-of-distribution tasks, even with random initialization.

papers.title: Chain-of-Goals Hierarchical Policy for Long-Horizon Offline Goal-Conditioned RL
papers.contribution: CoGHP consistently outperforms strong offline baselines on navigation and manipulation benchmarks, demonstrating improved performance on long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization for Primitive-Enabled Hierarchical RL: A Bilevel Approach
papers.contribution: DIPPER achieves up to 40% improvements over state-of-the-art baselines on challenging sparse-reward robotic navigation and manipulation benchmarks.

papers.title: Dreaming in Code for Curriculum Learning in Open-Ended Worlds
papers.contribution: Achieves 17% improvement in mean return over strongest baseline in Craftax, with non-zero success on late-game tasks where prior methods fail.

papers.title: Gradient-Aware Scheduling: Coupling Curriculum and Staleness for Async Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: GAS improves code generation Pass@1 from 39.7% to 60.1% while training at 2.3× the throughput of synchronous GRPO by matching each task's staleness budget to its loss-landscape curvature.

papers.title: Hierarchical Decision Making with Structured Policies: A Principled Design via Inverse Optimization
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms strong baselines in efficiency and decision quality on network resource allocation and continuous collision avoidance tasks.

papers.title: Hierarchical Entity-centric Reinforcement Learning with Factored Subgoal Diffusion
papers.contribution: Achieves over 150% higher success rates on hardest multi-entity tasks and generalizes to increasing horizons and entity counts.

papers.title: Hierarchical Goal Abstractions via Learned Subset Relations
papers.contribution: Agents achieve higher task success and greater generalization to novel tasks compared to agents using purely observational goals.

papers.title: Instance-wise Adaptive Scheduling via Derivative-Free Meta-Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms learning-based scheduling methods and instance-wise adaptation mechanisms under various task sizes and distributions.

papers.title: Learn to change the world: Multi-level reinforcement learning with model-changing actions
papers.contribution: We formalize a framework enabling agents to jointly optimize both configuration policies and primitive action policies to improve expected long-term reward.

papers.title: Learning Interpretable Options by Identifying Reward Diffusion Bottlenecks in Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: VPS efficiently discovers semantically meaningful subgoals in discrete tabular domains, continuous PointMaze, and Atari games, substantially improving exploration efficiency.

papers.title: Principled Fast and Meta Knowledge Learners for Continual Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on pixel-based and continuous control benchmarks for efficient cumulative knowledge transfer.

papers.title: Reflect-then-Correct: Rebalancing Task Optimization for Generalizable Meta-Reinforcement Learning via Distributional Value Error Reduction
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines on Meta-World ML-10 and ML-45 with theoretical guarantees for reweighting strategy.

papers.title: Strict Subgoal Execution: Reliable Long-Horizon Planning in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing goal-conditioned and hierarchical RL methods in efficiency and success rate across long-horizon benchmarks.

papers.title: Structure-Induced Information for Rerooting Levin Tree Search
papers.contribution: Scales to complex environments where explicit subgoal methods fail while achieving state-of-the-art online training efficiency.

papers.title: Structured Expert Routing with Multi-View Task Priors for Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: TGR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art offline meta-RL methods in few-shot generalization across continuous-control benchmarks, especially under sparse data and heterogeneous dynamics.

papers.title: TRACED: Transition-aware Regret Approximation with Co-learnability for Environment Design
papers.contribution: TRACED produces curricula that improve zero-shot generalization over strong baselines across multiple benchmarks with transition-prediction error driving rapid complexity ramp-up.

papers.title: Teaching Models to Teach Themselves: Reasoning at the Edge of Learnability
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that latent problem-generation ability emerges without requiring ability to solve hard problems, achieving improvements on zero-shot subsets of math benchmarks.

papers.title: The Cost of Commitment in Option-Based Hierarchical RL
papers.contribution: Characterizes optimal termination probabilities as a function of deliberation cost and error scale, clarifying behavior of popular HRL algorithms.

papers.title: Unsupervised Hierarchical Skill Discovery
papers.contribution: The method produces more structured and semantically meaningful skill hierarchies than baselines in pixel-based environments including Minecraft, and accelerates downstream RL tasks.
